Independent Islamic prep school, Tower Hamlets
One School Day. A Whole Education.
Qur'an, character and the full National Curriculum, taught together in classes of no more than 15. Daffodil Preparatory School is an independent Islamic day school for boys and girls in Tower Hamlets, taking children from age 2 at Daffodil Nursery through to Year 6.
No evening madrasah run, no split life. Your child's academic learning, Qur'an memorisation and daily Islamic practice all happen here, inside one coherent school day.
Member of the Independent Schools Association (ISA)
Inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI)
DfE Unique Reference Number 149148
A School Built Around Six Promises
Faith, Lived Daily
Every salah (obligatory prayer) that falls during school hours is prayed in congregation in our on-premise mosque. Mornings begin with adhkar and du'as (daily remembrances and supplications), and the timetable adjusts for Ramadan, including closing for the last ten days. Faith here is practised, not scheduled in later.
Serious Academics
We teach the full National Curriculum for England, alongside Islamic Studies, Arabic and basic Latin, chosen because it strengthens English grammar and underpins modern languages. Pupils sit all standardised assessments, from the phonics screening check to Key Stage 2 SATs (the national tests taken in Year 6), and have verbal and non-verbal reasoning lessons to prepare for secondary transfer.
The Hifdh Pathway
Hifdh, memorising the whole Qur'an, lives inside our timetable, not in a separate evening class. Children are grouped by ability, not age, across three levels: Beginner, Pre-Hifdh and Hifdh, with weekly memorisation assignments and termly assessments.
Small by Design
No class has more than 15 children. That cap is what makes the rest possible: regular one-to-one reading assessments, weekly quizzes in literacy and numeracy, and parent–teacher meetings every half term. Your child is known here: by name, by level, by character.
From 2 to 11, One Journey
Daffodil Nursery welcomes children from age 2, with government-funded hours available, and shares a site with the school. A child can join us as a toddler and leave us ready for secondary school: nine years of continuity, one set of values.
A Day That Works for Families
School runs 8:25am–3:30pm, Monday to Friday. The day doesn't have to end there. Homework Club, Debate Club for Key Stage 2 (Years 3–6), after-school care and a holiday Summer School help working families make the week add up.

The Results Behind the Promises
That result comes from a deliberate rhythm: weekly, monthly and termly internal assessments, one-to-one reading checks, and half-termly meetings with parents so nothing drifts unnoticed. How we assess and what our results show
Starting Younger? Begin at Daffodil Nursery
Our nursery takes children from age 2 to 5, follows the EYFS (Early Years Foundation Stage, the national framework for under-fives), and offers both government-funded and non-funded places. Nursery children grow up knowing the school they'll move into.
Who We Are, on the Record
We publish our inspection history in full and in plain terms. Read it on our Inspections & Standards page.

SEND & Inclusion
Some children need more from a school: more time, more patience, a different route to the same destination. This page explains how we approach special educational needs and disabilities (SEND), and why the conversation starts before your child does.
A Named SENCO You Can Actually Reach
Our SENCO (Special Educational Needs Coordinator, the member of staff responsible for SEND provision) is Stephen Montford, the headteacher. Email headteacher@daffodilprepschool.org.uk or call 020 4539 9737. In a school with classes of no more than 15, the person coordinating your child's support is also someone who knows your child.
We consider every application
We are an inclusive school. All applications are considered, including from children with SEND and children with an EHCP (Education, Health and Care Plan, the legal document setting out a child's assessed needs and the support they must receive).
The conversation comes first
Before any child joins us, we discuss their needs with you, openly and in both directions. We will ask about what helps your child and what doesn't; you should ask us whether we can genuinely provide it. Our admissions assessment exists to understand your child's current level so we can plan their provision. It is not a pass-or-fail entrance exam. We would rather have one honest conversation before entry than a difficult one afterwards.
How Small Classes and Constant Assessment Help
Identification and support are built into the school's normal rhythm, not bolted on.
No more than 15 in a class means a teacher can see, every day, how each child is actually doing, not just the loudest or the fastest.
Weekly, monthly and termly assessments, weekly literacy and numeracy quizzes, and regular one-to-one reading assessments mean a child who is struggling is noticed in weeks, not terms.
Half-termly parent–teacher meetings mean you hear about progress, and any emerging concern, six times a year and face to face, not once at a July parents' evening.
Documents and Local Support
Our SEND policy, with its version and review date, is available below and in the policy library.
For services, support and activities for children with SEND across the borough, see the Tower Hamlets Local Offer (external site).

Through the same rhythm every child gets: daily attention in a class of no more than 15, weekly quizzes, one-to-one reading assessments, and termly progress reviews. If a pattern emerges, the SENCO and class teacher discuss it. Then we talk to you.

Clubs, Competitions and the Life Around Lessons
A curriculum tells you what a school teaches. Enrichment tells you what a school loves. Ours runs from chess boards to debate podiums to Qur'an competitions. Everything happens on one site, inside or straight after the school day, so your child gets all of it without another journey across London.
Two Clubs That Anchor the Week
Homework Club
Homework done at school twice a week, with a teacher on hand. For children, it means help is there the moment they're stuck. For families, it means evenings can be about dinner and du'as rather than worksheet negotiations. Current days and times are shown below.
Debate Club (Key Stage 2)
For Years 3–6: structured debating that teaches children to build an argument, hear the other side and speak with confidence in front of others. It feeds naturally into our School Council, where pupils practise debate and leadership for real, with a say in the life of their own school. Current days and times are shown below.

Clubs are one part of a longer offer for working families: after-school provision, Homework Club and holiday Summer School together make the week workable. See how it fits together on our Wraparound Care page, and check the shape of the day on School Day & Term Dates.
See What Your Child Would Love Here
Every child finds a different favourite: the chessboard, the stage, the debate floor. Come and look around, ask about this year's clubs, and picture your child in them. Visits are individual, bookable by slot, and hosted by the headteacher.

Open Days at Daffodil
An open day is the sociable way to meet us: the school open to visiting families, the headteacher and staff on hand, and the chance to look around alongside other parents asking the same questions you are.
We run them periodically rather than to a fixed calendar. When one is scheduled, the date and RSVP form appear right here.
No Open Day on the Calendar Right Now, and You Don't Need One
You never have to wait for an event to see Daffodil. Our individual visits are the better look at the school: you book a slot, the headteacher hosts you personally, and you see ordinary lessons happening rather than a school dressed for visitors, with every question answered one-to-one.
If you'd rather come to an open day, send your details through the enquiry form and ask us to let you know when the next one is announced. We reply within 24 hours. Ask us anything
Why Families Come
Whether at an open day or an individual visit, you'll see the same school: classes capped at 15, salah prayed in congregation in our own mosque, and the full National Curriculum taught alongside a structured Qur'an pathway, all within one school day. The visit is where those sentences turn into things you've watched happen.

Care That Wraps Around the Working Week
A school that finishes at 3:30 only works for families if the day can go on when it needs to. Ours can. Wraparound care at Daffodil means your child stays in one familiar building, with familiar adults and familiar values: homework done, prayers prayed, halal food, no extra journey across London.
What's on Offer
Homework Club
Twice a week, homework gets done at school with a teacher on hand to help. Children go home with the work finished and understood; families get their evenings back. More on Homework Club and our other clubs.
After-school clubs and provision
Beyond Homework Club, after-school provision and clubs, including Debate Club for Key Stage 2, extend the day. What runs varies by term; the current schedule, days and prices are always shown below.
Holiday provision
School holidays are when working parents need us most, so our provision doesn't stop when term does. The centrepiece is Summer School.
Summer School
When the long holiday arrives, Daffodil Summer School gives children somewhere purposeful, safe and genuinely enjoyable to spend it, on the school site and run in the school's spirit.
What it's typically built around: a mix of learning that keeps term-time gains from fading and activities that make it feel nothing like school: creative projects, games, and days children actually ask to come back to. Faith stays part of the rhythm, as it does all year: du'as, salah and halal food.
Who it's for: school-age children who need somewhere good to be while parents work, and children who simply want to come. You don't have to need childcare to enjoy Summer School.
Dates, prices and booking: set for each holiday and published here as soon as they're confirmed.
Nursery Families
Wraparound questions start young. If your child is 2 to 5, Daffodil Nursery's own sessions are the starting point (see the Nursery pages). As they move up into school, the wraparound offer on this page takes over. One site, one system, from toddler to Year 6.
Build the Week Your Family Needs
Tell us your working pattern and we'll show you how the pieces fit around it: school day, clubs, Homework Club, holiday provision. Ask at a visit, or ring the office on 020 4539 9737 (8:00am–4:00pm, Monday to Friday).
Ask us anything. We reply within 24 hours. The shape of the day is on School Day & Term Dates.

Inspections & Standards
We tell you exactly where we are and where we are going. This page sets out our most recent inspection in full: every judgement, what it means, and what we have done since. No spin, in either direction.
Our September 2025 Inspection
Ofsted carried out our first graded inspection on 23–25 September 2025. The findings, in order:
Behaviour and attitudes: Good.
Personal development: Good.
Overall judgement: Requires Improvement.
Steps We Have Taken Since
We will not list promises here, only things that are already true and checkable:
We have moved to the ISI inspectorate. As a member of the Independent Schools Association (ISA), our future inspections will be carried out by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) rather than Ofsted.
We joined the Independent Schools Association (ISA), whose member schools commit to its standards of membership.
We run a structured assessment regime. All pupils sit the standardised national assessments, including the phonics screening check and Key Stage 1 and 2 SATs (the national tests taken in primary school), alongside internal weekly, monthly and termly assessments, weekly literacy and numeracy quizzes, regular one-to-one reading assessments, and half-termly parent–teacher meetings. Progress is measured constantly, not annually.
Safeguarding and SEND leadership is named and public. Our headteacher, Stephen Montford, is the school's Designated Safeguarding Lead and SENCO, and his contact route is published on our safeguarding and SEND pages.
How Independent Schools Are Inspected
Independent schools in England are inspected against the independent school standards set by the Department for Education. Two inspectorates do this work: Ofsted, which inspects most independent schools directly, and the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI), which is approved by the Department for Education to inspect schools belonging to the associations of the Independent Schools Council, including the ISA, of which we are a member. Both check the same underlying standards; they use different frameworks and report formats.
Our September 2025 inspection was carried out by Ofsted. Our future inspections will be carried out by ISI.
Read the Full Report
The complete report of our September 2025 inspection is available to download below. It is also published on Ofsted's website under our school record, URN 149148.
Then Judge Us in Person
A report is a three-day snapshot. A school is what happens on an ordinary Tuesday. Come and walk through ours: watch a lesson in a class of no more than 15, hear the Qur'an being learned, and put your hardest questions to the headteacher directly. He hosts every visit himself.
Or call 020 4539 9737. Prefer to write first? Ask us anything through our enquiry form. We reply within 24 hours.

The newsletter is how the week's school life reaches your kitchen table: what the children have been learning, dates you'll want on the calendar, reminders that save a scramble, and the small triumphs worth sharing. Every edition is published here as well as emailed, so nothing gets lost in an inbox.

Browse past editions below, newest first. If you're new to the school, the last few editions are an honest window into how the place actually feels week to week.
Get Each Edition by Email
Sign up and each new edition arrives in your inbox on the day it's published. This works for prospective parents too. It's a good way to watch the school from a distance while you decide.
Consent, plainly: Tick the box to confirm you'd like to receive Daffodil Preparatory School's newsletter by email. We'll use your email address for the newsletter and nothing else, we'll never sell or share it, and every edition includes an unsubscribe link that works first time. See our privacy notice for the full detail.
After you sign up, we'll send you a confirmation email. Click the link in it to complete your subscription (this double check protects you from being signed up by someone else). No confirmation click, no emails: simple.

Safeguarding
Nothing we do matters more than this. Every child at Daffodil has the right to feel safe, be safe, and know exactly which adult to talk to if something is wrong.
Our Commitment
We follow Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE), the statutory safeguarding guidance for all schools in England. In practice that means safeguarding is everyone's job here: all staff are trained to recognise concerns and know how to report them, and the wellbeing of the child comes before every other consideration.
At our most recent inspection (September 2025), safeguarding was judged effective. You can read that inspection in full on our Inspections & Standards page.
Who to Contact
Our Designated Safeguarding Lead (DSL, the senior member of staff responsible for child protection) is Stephen Montford, the headteacher.
Email: headteacher@daffodilprepschool.org.uk
Phone: 020 4539 9737 (ask for the headteacher; office hours are 8.00am–4.00pm, Monday to Friday)
If You Have a Concern
Safer Recruitment
We recruit carefully because the adults are the safeguard. All staff complete enhanced DBS checks (Disclosure and Barring Service, the national criminal-records check) and safer-recruitment vetting, including references, before they begin work with children, in line with KCSIE. See also our team and careers.
Read the full policy
Our safeguarding and child protection policy, with its version and review date, is available below and in the policy library. Printed copies are free from the school office.

Joining Daffodil: Five Clear Steps
We've kept admissions simple on purpose. Five steps, one named point of contact at each stage, and no surprises. Places are available in all year groups, and we accept children during the school year as well as in September. If you're moving school mid-year, you don't need to wait.
If your child is under 5, start with Daffodil Nursery, which takes children from age 2 and feeds naturally into Year 1.
The Journey at a Glance
Enquiry → Visit → Application → Assessment → Offer & Registration
Enquiry Tell us about your child: their age, the year group you have in mind, and when you'd like them to start. Use the short enquiry form, call 020 4539 9737, or email info@daffodilprepschool.org.uk. Our enquiry team replies within 24 hours. We publish that promise because we keep it. Ask us anything
Visit Next, come and see the school. Visits are individual, booked into a set slot, and hosted by the headteacher, Stephen Montford. You'll see classrooms, the mosque and the school in motion, and you can ask anything: fees, Hifdh levels, SEND support, results. Book a visit
Application When you're ready, apply through our online form. It takes you step by step through your child's details, health and SEN information, parent and emergency contacts, current schooling and documents. You can save your progress and come back later. A £100 registration fee per child is payable with the application; it is non-refundable. CMS/build: "Apply now" links here to the online application form when it ships (/admissions/apply/)
Assessment We invite your child in for an assessment. This is not a pass-or-fail entrance exam. Its purpose is to understand your child's current level in learning and, where relevant, Qur'an reading, so that if they join us they start in the right groups from day one. We consider every application, including from children with SEND (special educational needs and disabilities). If your child has an EHCP (Education, Health and Care Plan) or other identified needs, tell us early so we can talk honestly about the support we can offer. SEND at Daffodil
Offer & registration If we can offer your child a place, we'll confirm it in writing along with the start date and everything you need before the first morning. Where a year group is full, we hold a waiting list, and you may appeal in writing to the headteacher.
Joining Mid-year

Come and See a School Day Happen
A prospectus can tell you our class sizes. It can't show you fifteen children praying dhuhr together in their own mosque, or a Year 2 pupil reading one-to-one with their teacher. For that, you have to stand in the building.
That's why our visits are individual, not group tours. You book a slot, and the headteacher hosts you personally, so the person answering your questions about results, Hifdh levels, SEND support or fees is the person responsible for them.
What Your Visit Includes
Each visit runs to a booked slot; the available times and days are shown in the booking form below, so you'll see exactly what you're committing to before you choose.
The school in session. Classrooms during real lessons, so you see teaching, not a tidy empty room.
The spaces that make us different. The on-premise mosque, the science lab, the library and the IT room.
The Qur'an programme up close. How the Beginner, Pre-Hifdh and Hifdh levels work inside the timetable, and where your child would start.
A conversation with the headteacher, Stephen Montford. He is also our Designated Safeguarding Lead and SENCO, so questions about safeguarding and additional needs get first-hand answers.
Straight talk on admissions and fees. The five-step journey, what the assessment actually is, and the full fee picture, the same numbers we publish online.
Bring Your Child
Please do. Children usually decide about a school faster than adults, and watching yours react to the classrooms tells you more than any brochure. If you're also considering Daffodil Nursery for a younger sibling, mention it when you book and we'll cover both in one visit.
Booking Your Slot
Choose a time from the calendar below and tell us a little about your child: their age or year group and when you'd like to start. There are five short questions plus your slot; it takes about a minute.
Pick a slot, tell us about your child, and it's booked.
What Happens Once You've Booked
You'll get a confirmation email straight away with your date and time, a calendar file to save the slot, and a link to reschedule if something comes up. With young children, something often does. If anything about your booking needs a human, our enquiry team replies within 24 hours.
Prefer to arrange it by phone? Call 020 4539 9737 during office hours, Monday to Friday, 8am–4pm.
Can't make any of the slots?
Tell us what would work through the enquiry form and we'll try to accommodate you. If you'd rather see the school alongside other families first, check whether an open day is coming up.
After your visit
There's no follow-up pressure. When you're ready, the application form is online and takes seven short steps. Until then, the Admissions FAQ answers most of what parents ask on the way home.
Or call 020 4539 9737.

Admissions Questions, Answered Straight
These are the questions parents actually ask us: on visits, on the phone and on the way out of open days. We answer them plainly. If yours isn't here, use the enquiry form and we'll answer it within 24 hours.
Ages, Year Groups and Starting
Daffodil Preparatory School takes boys and girls aged 5 to 11, across Years 1 to 6 (Key Stages 1 and 2). Daffodil Nursery, on the same site, takes children from age 2 to 5, so a child can be with us continuously from 2 to 11.
Your child must be 5 by the start of the academic year to enter Year 1. If they're younger, Daffodil Nursery takes children from age 2 and follows the EYFS (the national framework for early years), with government-funded hours available for eligible families.
Naturally. The nursery shares a site with the school, so children grow up around the building, staff and rhythms they'll move into. Nursery families still complete the school application, and the Year 1 age rule applies: 5 by the start of the academic year.
Children can start in September or during the school year. You tell us your intended start when you enquire and choose the start term within the application form. In-year starters follow the same five-step journey as everyone else.
Joining and Applying
Yes. We accept in-year admissions, and places are currently available in all year groups. The process is the same five steps as a September start: enquiry, visit, application, assessment, then offer and registration. Because classes never exceed 15, children joining mid-year settle quickly.
No. There's no pass-or-fail entrance test. The assessment exists to understand your child's current level, academically and in their Qur'an reading, so they start in the right groups from the first morning. We consider every application, and the assessment shapes support, not selection.
We keep a waiting list and contact you as soon as a place opens in your child's year group. You can also appeal in writing to the headteacher. Right now, though, places are available in every year group, so ask before assuming a wait.
Three things: your child's passport (photo page), their birth certificate, and a recent proof of your home address. You upload them within the online application form, and clear phone photos are fine. If you're missing one, save the form and finish once you have it.
Fees and Costs
We publish our complete fee list on the Fees page: VAT-inclusive annual totals, the £100 registration fee, the sibling discount and payment by three termly instalments. No phone call needed, because every number is there in plain text.
The full uniform list, including PE kit, is on the uniform page. School jumpers and cardigans come through the school office, which can also tell you current prices for anything you need before your child starts, so there are no surprises in the first week.
School Life and Faith
No class at Daffodil has more than 15 children. That cap is deliberate: it's what allows regular one-to-one reading assessments, weekly literacy and numeracy quizzes, and parent–teacher meetings every half term, so no child's progress goes unnoticed.
Yes. All food at school is halal. Faith runs through the whole day here: every salah falling within school hours is prayed in congregation in our on-premise mosque, and mornings begin with adhkar and du'as.
The school timetable adjusts for Ramadan, and the school closes for the last ten days, protecting the nights that matter most for family worship. It's part of running a school around the Islamic year rather than squeezing the Islamic year around school.
The school day runs 8:25am–3:30pm, and around it we offer after-school provision including Homework Club, plus Debate Club for Key Stage 2, and a holiday Summer School. Current clubs, times and details are on the wraparound care page.
Support and Standards
Yes. We consider every application, including from children with special educational needs and disabilities, and those with an EHCP (Education, Health and Care Plan). Tell us about your child's needs early, ideally at enquiry, so we can talk honestly about the support we can offer. Our SENCO is the headteacher, Stephen Montford.
Our full inspection history is set out plainly on our Inspections & Standards page. It covers the September 2025 Ofsted outcome, including the Good judgements for behaviour and personal development, and our move to the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI).
Visits and Enquiries
Through the Book a Visit page, where you choose from set slots. Visits are individual rather than group tours, and the headteacher hosts each one personally. You're welcome to bring your child. Prefer the phone? Call 020 4539 9737 during office hours.
Within 24 hours. That's a published promise, not an aspiration. Every enquiry through the form, by email or by phone gets a reply from our enquiry team within one working day.
Still Deciding?
The honest next step is to see the school. Or just ask us the question that's stopping you.

How Payment Works
What your fees cover
Tuition fees cover the full taught day: the National Curriculum, Islamic Studies, the Qur'an and Hifdh programme, Arabic, Latin, and verbal and non-verbal reasoning lessons. All of it sits inside school hours, so there's no separate madrasah fee on top of school fees. Optional extras such as clubs, wraparound care and the Summer School are booked separately; current details are on the wraparound care page. Uniform is bought separately. See the uniform page.
Bursaries and scholarships
We don't offer bursaries or scholarships. Instead, we put our effort into keeping the published fee within reach, roughly £350–£365 a month across the year including VAT. We publish it in full, so families can plan with real numbers rather than apply and hope.
Withdrawal and the fees policy
If you withdraw your child, we ask for a full term's written notice. Fees are non-refundable and non-transferable, and late payment may incur administration fees. The full detail lives in our fees policy:
Fees Policy
August 2026 (v3.0) · 16 September 2026 · 135 KB
Fees FAQ
The fee list is set exclusive of VAT, and 20% VAT applies to independent school fees. That's why we publish both columns: Years 1–2 come to approximately £4,200 per year including VAT, and Years 3–6 to approximately £4,380. The inclusive figure is the one to budget on.
Fees are payable in three termly instalments across the year, as shown in the table above. If you're working out a monthly equivalent for budgeting, the VAT-inclusive annual fee spreads to roughly £350–£365 a month over twelve months.
No. The only payment before an offer is the £100 registration fee, paid per child when you apply. It is non-refundable, but there is no additional deposit at offer or registration stage.
Yes. A £250 sibling discount applies when more than one of your children attends Daffodil. There is also a £250 referral reward when a family you introduce joins the school, subject to terms and conditions. Ask the office how both are applied.
No. We keep our published fees as low as we can for every family rather than discounting for a few, and we publish them in full, including VAT, so you can compare us accurately with other schools.
A full term's written notice. Fees already paid are non-refundable and non-transferable, and late payments may incur administration fees. The fees policy, downloadable above, sets out the exact terms.
Uniform is bought separately. Optional provision (clubs, after-school care, the Summer School) is booked and charged separately, with current details on the relevant pages. Within the taught day itself, the Qur'an and Hifdh programme is part of the curriculum, not a paid extra.
Daffodil Nursery is priced separately and offers both government-funded hours and non-funded places for children aged 2 to 5. Current rates and funding routes are explained on the nursery funding and fees page. Start there, then contact us with your child's age.
The Next Step
You've seen the numbers. Now see the school, or apply today if you're ready.

The Full National Curriculum, and More Besides
Your child follows the complete National Curriculum for England across Key Stage 1 (Years 1–2) and Key Stage 2 (Years 3–6): the same subjects, standards and national tests as any good primary school. Then we add what most primary schools don't: a structured Qur'an programme inside the timetable, Islamic Studies woven through the day, Latin for every pupil and reasoning lessons that prepare children for secondary transfer.
All of it happens in classes of no more than 15, so teachers know exactly where each child is. They can prove it too, with weekly quizzes and regular one-to-one reading assessments.
The National Curriculum, Subject by Subject
English
Reading, writing, spelling, grammar and spoken language, from early phonics in Key Stage 1 through to sustained independent writing in Year 6. Weekly literacy quizzes and regular one-to-one reading assessments mean no child's reading drifts unnoticed. Writing competitions and bookmaking projects give children real reasons to write well.
Mathematics
Number, calculation, fractions, geometry, measurement and statistics, building step by step towards the Key Stage 2 SATs (the national tests taken in Year 6). Weekly numeracy quizzes check that each step has stuck before the next one is built on it. Maths challenges and logic puzzles stretch children who are ready for more.
Science
Biology, chemistry and physics topics taught through observation, questioning and hands-on investigation in our own science lab. STEM (science, technology, engineering and maths) is a deliberate focus of the school, in lessons and in our STEM challenges beyond them.
Computing and Design & Technology
Children learn to use technology purposefully and to understand how it works, from early algorithms and simple programs through to designing, making and evaluating their own projects. Our IT room supports regular, hands-on computing lessons.
Art & Design
Drawing, painting, making and the study of artists and designers. Art sits alongside music and drama in the life of the school, and children's creative work feeds into end-of-term projects and productions.
Geography
Place knowledge, physical and human geography, fieldwork and map skills, starting with the local area and widening to the UK, Europe and the world.
History
A chronological understanding of British and world history, brought to life through educational trips to museums and historical sites.
Physical Education
Regular PE develops fitness, coordination and teamwork, and the year includes sports days the whole school looks forward to. PE kit details are on our Uniform page.
Languages
Children study a modern foreign language (French, Spanish or Arabic), developing listening, speaking, reading and writing. Arabic carries a particular weight here: it is the language of the Qur'an your child is learning to recite and memorise.
What We Add to the National Curriculum
Islamic Studies, Woven Through the Day
Islamic Studies is not a Friday afternoon add-on. Children learn fiqh (Islamic jurisprudence), hadith (the recorded words and actions of the Prophet ﷺ), sirah (the life of the Prophet ﷺ) and akhlaq and adab (character and manners). They then live what they learn, in daily adhkar and du'as and in salah prayed in congregation in our on-premise mosque. How faith runs through the school day
Basic Latin, for Every Pupil
Every child learns basic Latin. Not for tradition's sake: Latin is the root of the modern languages children go on to study, and it strengthens their command of English grammar. A child who has met Latin cases and verb endings understands their own language more precisely.
Verbal and Non-verbal Reasoning
From word logic to pattern and spatial problems, reasoning lessons build the thinking skills that 11+ and secondary-transfer assessments test. Year 6 children walk into those assessments having practised the format for years, not weeks.
How We Know It's Working
The curriculum is checked constantly, not annually. Weekly quizzes in literacy and numeracy, monthly and termly assessments, one-to-one reading assessments and half-termly parent-teacher meetings keep every child's progress visible, to us and to you. Pupils sit all standardised national assessments, including the phonics screening check and Key Stage 1 and 2 SATs.
How we assess, and what our results show
Curriculum maps
Each year group's curriculum map shows what your child will study, term by term. Current maps are available to download below.
Beyond the classroom
Chess tournaments, debating through the School Council, themed term projects, trips, arts and more. See the full picture on our Clubs & Enrichment page. And for children starting younger, the journey begins with the EYFS (Early Years Foundation Stage) at Daffodil Nursery.

A curriculum page can tell you what we teach. A morning here shows you how. Visits are individual, bookable by slot, and hosted by the headteacher.

Careers at Daffodil
If you became a teacher to actually know the children you teach, a class of no more than 15 changes the job. Here is what working at Daffodil is like, what we are looking for, and exactly what happens after you apply.
Why Work Here
Before applying, read about the school and our Inspections & Standards page. We publish our position honestly and expect candidates to arrive informed.
Classes capped at 15. You can hear every reader read, mark meaningfully, and adapt lessons to the children in front of you, not manage a crowd.
A school still being built. We opened in 2022 and are growing year on year. Staff who join now shape how things are done, rather than inheriting how they have always been done.
A faith-filled working day. Salah is prayed in congregation in our on-premise mosque, the day opens with adhkar, food is halal, and the timetable respects Ramadan, including closure for its last ten days.
Serious about STEM and the whole curriculum. We teach the full National Curriculum with a STEM focus, plus Qur'an, Arabic, Islamic Studies and basic Latin. There is interesting work here for specialists and generalists alike.

How We Recruit: Safer Recruitment

pageCache.text:
An Islamic Beginning, from Age 2
Daffodil Nursery · Ages 2–5
Daffodil Nursery welcomes children aged 2 to 5 into a warm, unhurried Islamic environment on the same site as Daffodil Preparatory School, in Tower Hamlets. Days are built around the EYFS (the Early Years Foundation Stage, the national framework for children under five): learning through play, guided by adults who know that at this age, feeling safe comes before everything else.
And gently, from the very start, faith is part of the day. Children learn their daily du'as (supplications), hear the Qur'an recited beautifully, and begin the first, softest foundations of their own Qur'an journey. Nothing forced. Everything familiar.
What Your Child's Early Years Look Like Here
Learning Through Play
Following the EYFS: communication and language, physical development, early literacy and numeracy, and the personal, social and emotional growth that underpins all of it.
Faith Woven in Gently
Daily du'as, the sounds and rhythms of the Qur'an, and the beginnings of Islamic character: kindness, sharing, saying bismillah before meals.
Halal Food, Always
Food served at nursery is halal, always.
Attention, Not Crowds
Like the school it belongs to, this nursery is built around children being known: by name, by temperament, by what made them laugh this morning. Small enough to notice; close enough to care.
Settling in, Gently
Starting nursery is a big step, usually bigger for parents than for children. We take settling in seriously and take it at your child's pace, working with you as partners: you know your child, we know the room, and together we get the start right. Tears at the door are normal; our job is to make them brief.
Curious what the hours in between actually hold? Walk through one on our Nursery Day page.
Funded and Non-funded Places
Daffodil Nursery offers both government-funded places, using the funded early-education hours available to eligible families, and non-funded (private) places. Which route fits your family depends on your circumstances, and we've set it out plainly, with links to the official checkers, on our Funding & Fees page.
One Journey, from 2 to 11
This is what makes Daffodil Nursery different from a standalone nursery: it's the first chapter of a nine-year story. Nursery children share a site with the Preparatory School, grow up seeing the school they'll move into, and can continue into Year 1 without changing buildings, values or community. By the time your child starts school, school isn't a strange place. It's just upstairs from their childhood.
From here, the path runs through the full National Curriculum and a structured Qur'an programme to age 11. See where the journey leads · The Qur'an and hifdh pathway
Come and Meet Us
Choosing a nursery is a gut decision as much as a checklist one. You'll know when you stand in the room. Visits are individual, bookable by slot, and hosted by the headteacher.
Ask us anything: we reply within 24 hours · Call 020 4539 9737

Funded and Non-funded Places, Explained Plainly
Daffodil Nursery offers two routes in: government-funded places, using the funded early-education hours many families are entitled to, and non-funded (private) places for families who want hours beyond or outside the funded scheme. This page explains both, without jargon, and points you to the official tools for checking what you're entitled to.
The Funded Route: Government-funded Childcare Hours
The government funds early education and childcare for families in England. The scheme is national: the rules are the same at every provider. Under the current scheme it works like this:
Funded hours are generally based on 38 weeks of the year (term time), and providers may charge for extras such as meals. The definitive, up-to-date rules, and the application itself, live at Childcare Choices, the government's official childcare support site.
How to check and apply
Local, human help is available too: the Tower Hamlets Family Information Service offers free advice on childcare and funding for families in the borough.
The Non-funded Route: Private Places
Not every family fits the funded scheme, and some want more than it covers. Non-funded places are straightforward private sessions, paid directly to the nursery. Current session options and rates are shown below and are always available from the school office.
Many families combine the two routes: funded hours plus additional private sessions. Tell us what your week needs and we'll set out exactly how it would work, in writing, before you commit to anything.
Frequently Asked Questions
Curious what those hours feel like once your child is in the room? Read about a day at the nursery, or start at the Nursery overview.
Use the official checker at childcarechoices.gov.uk. It asks about your work, income and your child's age, and gives you a definitive answer in minutes. Broadly, both parents (or a lone parent) need to be working and within the scheme's income rules, but the checker is the source of truth.
Possibly, through either route. Eligible working families can access funded hours from 9 months old, so a 2-year-old can qualify that way. Separately, some 2-year-olds qualify for 15 hours through additional support, for example where a family receives certain benefits. Check both at childcarechoices.gov.uk.
Then the non-funded route is yours: private sessions, paid directly, with current rates available from the office and shown on this page. And remember that all 3- and 4-year-olds get 15 universal funded hours regardless of work status, so a fully private arrangement often becomes partly funded later.
Yes, this is common. Your funded entitlement covers part of the week and private sessions cover the rest. We'll map your entitlement against the sessions you need and confirm the exact arrangement, and any costs, in writing before your child starts.
The funded hours cover early education and care during those hours. Nationally, providers may charge for extras such as meals. We'll be completely transparent about anything that applies here before you accept a place. You'll never meet a cost you weren't told about.
Earlier than feels necessary. Working-families codes apply from the term after you become eligible, so apply in the term before you want your child to start, and reconfirm your code with HMRC when prompted. If the timing is confusing, call us. We help families with this constantly.
Talk It Through with Us
Funding rules are national; children are individual. Come and see the nursery, bring your questions about hours and costs, and leave with a clear picture. Visits are individual, bookable by slot, and hosted by the headteacher.

pageCache.pageTitle: A Day at Our Nursery | Daffodil Nursery
pageCache.text:
A Day at Daffodil Nursery
No two days with small children are identical. That is rather the point of small children. But a good nursery day has a shape a child can trust: the same welcome, the same rhythms, the same faces. Here is the shape of ours. Current session times and drop-off arrangements are shown below.
Session times and drop-off/collection windows are managed in the CMS and always shown current here.
Arriving
The day starts with a proper welcome: a familiar adult, at child height, who knows your child's name and yesterday's triumphs. Handovers are unhurried: if there's something we should know (a bad night, a wobbly tooth, a new baby at home), the door is where you tell us.
Learning Through Play
The morning belongs to play, which, under the EYFS (Early Years Foundation Stage, the national framework for under-fives), is how young children genuinely learn. Building, pouring, painting, pretending, singing, listening to stories: through it all, adults are extending language, counting the blocks as they topple, and noticing what each child is ready for next. There is structure underneath the play; your child just experiences the play.
Woven gently through the day are the first threads of faith: daily du'as (supplications) said together, bismillah before food, alhamdulillah after it, and the sound of the Qur'an as something beautiful and familiar. At this age, faith is caught more than taught, so we make it warm, sung and shared.
Meals and Snacks
All food at the nursery is halal. Mealtimes are social, unrushed and gently supervised. Children learn to sit together, try things, and manage their own spoons with growing dignity. Tell us about allergies and preferences before your child starts, and we'll agree exactly how we'll handle them.
Rest and quiet
Little bodies need real rest. The day includes quiet time, and younger children who still nap can sleep. We follow your child's own rhythm and your guidance, not a one-size-fits-all schedule. A rested child spends the afternoon playing; an exhausted one spends it crying. We know which afternoon we'd rather give you back.
The afternoon, and home time
Afternoons bring more play, often outdoors: energy activities, stories and songs to gather everyone back together. At collection, you get a real handover, not a wave: what your child did, ate, and delighted in. For the days when you can't be there yourself, tell us in advance who will be. We release children only to adults you've named.
What to Bring
Not much, honestly. Before your child starts we'll give you a short, simple list: named spare clothes and anything that helps your child feel settled. Label everything with your child's name; two-year-olds are magnificent at wearing other people's jumpers home.
Settling in: a partnership, not a policy
Every child settles differently, so we plan the start together, with you. Some children stride in on day one; some need a gentler, more gradual beginning with a parent nearby. We'll follow your child's cues and keep talking to you until drop-off is boring, which, in nursery terms, is what success looks like.
If you're weighing up costs and funded hours alongside all this, our Funding & Fees page sets it out plainly. For everything else about the nursery, start at the Nursery overview.
The Best Way to Feel a Day Is to Stand in One
Come during a session. See the room mid-play, hear the du'as before snack, and picture your child in the middle of it. Visits are individual, bookable by slot, and hosted by the headteacher.
